labels.app_caption: Local-first writing feedback for quick classroom review.
labels.local_notice: Language and sentiment analysis run locally. Journalistic angle generation sends your text and prompt to CSCS Apertus only when you click Generate.
labels.input_placeholder: Paste up to a few pages of writing here.
labels.empty_text: Please paste some text before running the analysis.
labels.grade_help: Flesch-Kincaid grade is shown for English only. French text uses French reading ease; its grade is marked N/A.
labels.reading_help: Reading ease is higher when prose is easier to scan quickly.
labels.presence_help: Executive presence here is a heuristic score based on readability, repetition, and sentiment intensity; it is not a validated assessment.
labels.external_ai: Use External AI Without Sharing Your Key
labels.external_ai_help: For richer critique, copy the prompt below into an AI tool of your choice. The Journalistic Angle tab can also send your text to the configured CSCS API.
labels.ai_detection_notice: I have not wired in an automatic AI-authorship detector. The better-looking API options are paid or English-only, and I would not trust them enough to make this part feel authoritative for student evaluation.
labels.angle_intro: Explore combinations to choose a journalistic angle.
labels.angle_missing: The angle-machine HTML file could not be found.
labels.angle_companion: Wheel selections are not copied here automatically. Use the menus below to compose your angle proposal.
labels.angle_help: Best fit: treat this as a planning companion for journalism/story framing, separate from the writing-quality analysis above.
labels.diagnostics_help: These are extra revision checks. They are not separate apps or AI tools, just local signals that help you inspect structure, wording, and tone.
labels.paragraph_help: `Paragraphs` and `Longest Paragraph` help you see whether the draft is visually broken up or hiding large blocks of text.
labels.lexical_help: `Unique Words` and `Lexical Diversity` give a rough sense of vocabulary variety. Higher is not always better.
labels.passive_help: `Passive Voice Flags` relies on syntactic dependency patterns to identify passive constructions.
labels.hedge_help: `Hedging Words` counts softeners in the selected language, such as `perhaps` or `peut-être`.
labels.transition_help: `Transitions Found` looks for connectors in the selected language, such as `however` or `cependant`.
labels.angle_prompt: Analyze the text for a simple journalistic angle. Identify the central news value, the most compelling perspective, who is affected, and one concise angle to pursue. Be specific and grounded only in the supplied text; note important missing information. Respond in English.
labels.empty_request: Paste some text before requesting an analysis.
labels.style_readable: Sentence length is generally in a readable range.
labels.style_rhythm: Review sentence rhythm: average length falls outside the 12–22 word range.
labels.style_no_long: No overloaded long sentences were detected.
labels.style_long: Consider splitting the longest sentences to make their main point easier to follow.
labels.style_no_repetition: Word repetition is limited, which helps the draft feel less redundant.
labels.style_punctuation: Punctuation use reads as controlled rather than overly dramatic.
labels.style_intensity: Punctuation may be adding extra intensity; review exclamation marks and rhetorical questions.
labels.style_short: Very short sentences appear in the draft; make sure they are intentional for emphasis.
labels.no_strengths: - No standout strengths were identified by the local ruleset.
labels.no_revision_flags: - No major local revision flags were raised.
labels.pos_help: Select one or more word classes to highlight matching words in your submitted text. Verb includes auxiliary verbs.
labels.spacy_error: spaCy could not load. Run `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` in the app's environment and restart the app.
labels.sentiment_empty: Enter some text to see sentiment scores.
labels.shares_help: Shares describe VADER's sentiment proportions, not confidence probabilities or exact percentages of words.
labels.mean_help: The mean gives every sentence equal weight. It is separate from the document compound score.
labels.mixed_sentiment: Both positive and negative sentences occur here. A single document score can hide that mixture.
labels.vader_explanation: VADER uses a sentiment dictionary and rules for negation, intensifiers, capitals, and punctuation. Compound runs from −1 (negative) to +1 (positive). Near zero can mean little emotional wording or opposing signals that cancel; it does not prove objectivity.
labels.vader_limits: Use the sentence chart to locate shifts and review the actual passages. Quotes and descriptions of bad events can score negatively without the author taking a negative stance. Sarcasm, implied meaning, and domain-specific language can be missed. These scores do not measure writing quality, factual accuracy, or political bias.
labels.vader_french: French uses a separate VADER adaptation with a translated lexicon. Its scores are not calibrated to be directly comparable with English scores.
labels.api_key_missing: CSCS_INFERENCE_API_KEY is not configured. Add it to .env or the environment.
labels.api_invalid: The inference API returned an invalid response.
labels.api_no_analysis: The inference API response did not contain an analysis.
labels.language_fallback: The language could not be identified as English or French (detected: {detected}). Using French by default; you can select the language in Settings.
labels.summary_counts: This draft is about {words} words across {sentences} sentences.
labels.summary_grade: The readability estimate is around grade {grade:.1f}, with an average sentence length of {average:.1f} words.
labels.summary_ease: French reading ease is {ease:.1f}, with an average sentence length of {average:.1f} words.
labels.summary_sentiment: VADER classifies the document’s emotional wording as {label}; this is not a judgment of writing quality or author intent.
labels.style_repetition: Check whether these repeated words are needed: {terms}.
labels.pos_summary: {total} words highlighted ({selection}). Verbs: {verbs} · Nouns: {nouns} · Adverbs: {adverbs} · Adjectives: {adjectives}
labels.pos_model_error: The {language} language model could not load. Run `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` in the app's environment and restart the app.
labels.sentiment_load_error: {language} sentiment support could not load. Run `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` in the app's environment and restart the app.
labels.api_connection_error: Could not reach the inference API: {reason}
labels.angle_starter: Build this as a {time} {format} piece. Lead with a {focus} frame, using a {perspective} perspective. The target effect is {function_1} through {function_2}.
labels.angle_credit: The Angle Machine (v1.77) © Andrew Robotham, Academy of Journalism and Media
labels.ai_prompt:
You are helping a student improve a piece of writing.

Language of input: {language_code}
Expected response language: {language}

Please analyze the writing below and return:
1. A 3-sentence executive summary.
2. Top 3 strengths.
3. Top 3 weaknesses.
4. Notes on executive presence, clarity, and tone.
5. Concrete revision suggestions.

Writing:
"""
{text}
"""
labels.empty_prompt: Please enter a prompt before requesting an analysis.
labels.spacy_breakdown_help: Token annotations include lemmas, fine-grained tags, syntax, morphology and named entities. POS, dependency and morphology shares use all non-space tokens; entity shares use entity mentions. VERB and AUX are separate here.
labels.no_annotations: No matching annotations in this text.
labels.average_sentence_help: Average number of words per sentence.
labels.lexical_ratio_help: Unique word forms divided by total words. Higher is not necessarily better.
